title: Why Agent Evaluation Is Harder Than Model Evaluation

content_html:
I did not get to this opinion from a whitepaper.

I got to it because I am building an open-source project around the problem, and the build keeps arguing back.

I am working on AgentEval Forge right now, an OSS evaluation lab for agents. The original idea sounded straightforward enough: scenario packs, adversarial cases, trajectory scoring, regression tracking, cost and latency analysis. In my head, it was going to be a more serious, more structured version of evaluation work I had already done elsewhere.

That was the first mistake.

I had already spent time building model-eval and workload-eval style systems. I knew what it meant to compare models for real tasks, how to design rubrics, how to think about speed versus cost, and how quickly a neat score can become misleading if the harness is weak. I assumed agent evaluation would be an extension of that same world.

The deeper I got into AgentEval Forge, the less true that felt.

Model evaluation asks whether the answer is good.

Agent evaluation has to ask whether the system behaved well enough to trust.

Those are not the same question.

The comparison that made it click

A clean model-eval setup is something I know how to reason about. You have an input, an output, and some way of scoring quality. Sometimes that is exact match. Sometimes it is a rubric. Sometimes it is an LLM judge. Sometimes it is a benchmark harness. However fancy the setup gets, the center of gravity is still pretty stable: did the model produce a good answer for this task?

That is already hard enough. I have seen enough brittle scoring and false confidence to know that even model evaluation can go wrong in ways that look scientific. A rubric can reward the wrong thing. A binary check can miss something obviously useful. A benchmark can feel objective while still pulling you toward the wrong optimization target. So I am not pretending model eval is solved.

But with agents, the shape of the problem changes.

The thing being evaluated is no longer just an answer. It is a workflow. It is a sequence of decisions. It is tool choice, retries, intermediate state, cost, recovery behavior, and sometimes policy adherence. The moment you let a system do more than respond once, the final output stops being the whole story.

That sounds obvious when you say it plainly. In practice, I think a lot of teams still use answer-scoring habits on systems that have already moved past that category.

What changed for me while building AgentEval Forge

The real shift happened when I tried to define what AgentEval Forge would actually have to score.

At first, I thought the answer would be simple: run scenario packs, score the outputs, compare versions, done.

But the more I looked at real agent behavior, the more that started to feel naive. An agent can produce a decent final answer while doing a lot of things badly on the way there. It can choose the wrong tool first and recover by luck. It can loop more than it should. It can spend five times the tokens a better path would spend. It can take a risky step that a human reviewer would never approve, then still back into something that looks acceptable at the end.

If I only score the final answer, I might mark that run as a success.

That is the trap.

The path matters.

That is the sentence I keep coming back to while building this. The path matters just as much as the endpoint, and sometimes more, because the path is where cost, safety, and trust actually live.

That challenge shows up in very practical ways. I am not just trying to score whether an agent got the answer right. I am thinking about cases where it picked the wrong tool first, passed the task only because it recovered late, crossed a boundary it should not have crossed, spent too many steps on something simple, or regressed only inside one narrow scenario family while the average score still looked fine. That is the kind of mess that makes agent evaluation feel much more like systems work than answer grading.

I had already seen hints of this in earlier work

This was not the first time I had felt the edges of the problem.

In earlier harness and field-study work, especially when running systems against real workloads instead of toy examples, I kept finding failures that would never have shown up in a neat prompt-eval setup. That experience made me much less impressed by demo-path confidence.

A system can look strong in a controlled evaluation and then become erratic as soon as the environment gets irregular. Real repos. Real logs. Real commit histories. Real naming mess. Real ambiguity.

That is where edge cases show up. That is where tool misuse shows up. That is where “technically correct” and “safe to ship” start to drift apart.

I think that history is part of why AgentEval Forge took the shape it did in my head. I was not trying to build a leaderboard generator. I was trying to build something that feels closer to release discipline for agents.

Not: did this run look good?

More like: if I change this system, what got better, what got worse, what got more expensive, and what became riskier even if the top-line score improved?

That feels much more like engineering than benchmarking.

The five things I now think agent evaluation has to cover

The more I think about it, the more I come back to five dimensions.

First, you still need final correctness. If the agent does not solve the task, the rest only matters so much.

Second, you need trajectory quality. How did it get there? Was the sequence of decisions sensible, efficient, and stable? Or did it succeed in a way you would never want repeated in production?

Third, you need to evaluate tool behavior. Did it choose the right tools? Did it overuse them? Did it take expensive or risky actions unnecessarily? Did it rely on accidental recovery?

Fourth, you need safety and policy adherence. A successful output reached through an unsafe path should not count as a clean win.

Fifth, you need cost, latency, and regressions. Did the new version get slower? More expensive? More erratic? Did it improve accuracy while making operational behavior worse? Did it just change style and still get celebrated as progress?

That last one matters a lot to me because I think it is where teams fool themselves most easily. They see difference and call it improvement. Those are not the same thing.

Why I do not think the current eval ecosystem is enough

I am not arguing that the current eval ecosystem is useless. Far from it.

The LangChain piece on evaluation-driven development gets a core thing right: once you see failures in production, those failures need to feed offline evals, and every change should be tested against them. That loop is healthy. It is exactly the kind of discipline I want more teams to adopt.

And from a different angle, Birgitta Böckeler's writing on agentic coding captures something else I think matters: the most dangerous failures often live in longer feedback loops. Maintainability. Team friction. Brute-force fixes. Misdiagnosis. Overbuilt solutions. Those costs do not always show up in the immediate output, but they absolutely show up later.

That is why I do not think the issue is that existing tools are bad. I think the issue is that many of our evaluation habits were formed in a prompt-and-answer world. Agent systems are messier. They behave more like orchestrated software than isolated text generation. Once you accept that, your evaluation system has to grow up too.

Even the eval can lie to you

This is the part I do not want to over-neaten.

Your evaluation setup can be wrong in ways that feel rigorous.

I have already seen enough of that in model-eval and harness work to be wary of any system that sounds more certain than it really is. You can undercount useful behavior. You can make your binary checks too brittle. You can optimize for what is easy to score rather than what actually matters.

So now the challenge has two layers. The agent is hard to evaluate, and the evaluation system itself becomes another system you have to design carefully, calibrate honestly, and distrust a little.

That is not a reason to avoid serious evaluation. If anything, it is the opposite. It means evaluation has to be treated like product and engineering work, not just like reporting.

Why I am still optimistic about building this

For all of that, I do not feel cynical about the problem.

If anything, building AgentEval Forge has made me more convinced that this is worth doing well. I want scenario packs. I want adversarial cases. I want trajectory scoring. I want regression tracking that can tell me which change made the system more useful and which one only made it look cleaner in a demo.

I want an evaluation system that helps answer a release question, not just a research question.

Did this version get better?

Better how?

At what cost?

And what got riskier even if the headline score went up?

That is the kind of question I want tooling to help with.

The bigger thing I think teams are about to learn

I suspect a lot of teams are still doing with agent evaluation what many teams did with AI-assisted coding more broadly: borrowing habits from an earlier problem and hoping they scale.

Sometimes they do.

Often they do not.

And then the bill shows up later, in regressions, strange production behavior, expensive paths, unsafe tool use, or a team that keeps changing the system without ever being able to say whether it actually improved.

That is why this topic feels worth writing about while I am still in the middle of building the OSS for it. The build itself is sharpening the argument for me. Every design decision keeps pushing me toward the same conclusion: model evaluation asks whether the answer is good. Agent evaluation has to ask whether the system behaved well enough to trust.

That is a harder problem. I think it is also going to become one of the defining engineering problems of serious agent work.

I will write more about this once the OSS is public. Some of these challenges are already turning into concrete design decisions in AgentEval Forge, and in the coming weeks I want to share which parts we solved cleanly, which parts stayed messy, and how the tradeoffs changed once the code had to work as a real system instead of an idea. I will share the GitHub repo publicly when that is ready.

Open for discussion

This is still an active build and an active line of thinking for me, so I would genuinely like pushback on it.

  • Where did answer scoring stop being enough for your agent work?
  • Are you evaluating the path yet, or still mostly the final output?
  • What has been hardest to score well: tool use, regressions, safety, cost, or something else?
  • And the big one: are we building evaluation systems that improve release confidence, or just better ways to feel rigorous?

sentences.zh: 它可能会采取人类审阅者永远不会批准的冒险步骤，然后仍然回到最终看起来可以接受的东西。

blocks.html_en: If I only score the final answer, I might mark that run as a success.

sentences.en: If I only score the final answer, I might mark that run as a success.
sentences.zh: 如果我只得到最终答案，我可能会将这次运行标记为成功。

blocks.html_en: That is the trap.

sentences.en: That is the trap.
sentences.zh: 这就是陷阱。

blocks.html_en: The path matters.

sentences.en: The path matters.
sentences.zh: 道路很重要。

blocks.html_en: That is the sentence I keep coming back to while building this. The path matters just as much as the endpoint, and sometimes more, because the path is where cost, safety, and trust actually live.

sentences.en: That is the sentence I keep coming back to while building this.
sentences.zh: 这就是我在构建此项目时不断回想起的一句话。

sentences.en: The path matters just as much as the endpoint, and sometimes more, because the path is where cost, safety, and trust actually live.
sentences.zh: 路径与端点一样重要，有时甚至更重要，因为路径是成本、安全和信任的实际所在。

blocks.html_en: That challenge shows up in very practical ways. I am not just trying to score whether an agent got the answer right. I am thinking about cases where it picked the wrong tool first, passed the task only because it recovered late, crossed a boundary it should not have crossed, spent too many steps on something simple, or regressed only inside one narrow scenario family while the average score still looked fine. That is the kind of mess that makes agent evaluation feel much more like systems work than answer grading.

sentences.en: That challenge shows up in very practical ways.
sentences.zh: 这一挑战以非常实际的方式显现出来。

sentences.en: I am not just trying to score whether an agent got the answer right.
sentences.zh: 我不仅仅是想对代理人的答案是否正确进行评分。

sentences.en: I am thinking about cases where it picked the wrong tool first, passed the task only because it recovered late, crossed a boundary it should not have crossed, spent too many steps on something simple, or regressed only inside one narrow scenario family while the average score still looked fine.
sentences.zh: 我正在考虑这样的情况：它首先选择了错误的工具，仅因为恢复较晚而通过了任务，跨越了不应该跨越的边界，在简单的事情上花费了太多步骤，或者仅在一个狭窄的场景系列中回归，而平均分数看起来仍然不错。

sentences.en: That is the kind of mess that makes agent evaluation feel much more like systems work than answer grading.
sentences.zh: 这种混乱使得代理评估感觉更像是系统工作而不是答案评分。

blocks.html_en: I had already seen hints of this in earlier work

sentences.en: I had already seen hints of this in earlier work
sentences.zh: 我在早期的工作中已经看到了这方面的暗示

blocks.html_en: This was not the first time I had felt the edges of the problem.

sentences.en: This was not the first time I had felt the edges of the problem.
sentences.zh: 这不是我第一次感受到问题的边缘。

blocks.html_en: In earlier harness and field-study work, especially when running systems against real workloads instead of toy examples, I kept finding failures that would never have shown up in a neat prompt-eval setup. That experience made me much less impressed by demo-path confidence.

sentences.en: In earlier harness and field-study work, especially when running systems against real workloads instead of toy examples, I kept finding failures that would never have shown up in a neat prompt-eval setup.
sentences.zh: 在早期的利用和现场研究工作中，特别是在针对实际工作负载而不是玩具示例运行系统时，我不断发现在简洁的提示评估设置中永远不会出现的故障。

sentences.en: That experience made me much less impressed by demo-path confidence.
sentences.zh: 那次经历让我对演示路径的信心不再那么印象深刻。

blocks.html_en: A system can look strong in a controlled evaluation and then become erratic as soon as the environment gets irregular. Real repos. Real logs. Real commit histories. Real naming mess. Real ambiguity.

sentences.en: A system can look strong in a controlled evaluation and then become erratic as soon as the environment gets irregular.
sentences.zh: 一个系统在受控评估中可能看起来很强大，但一旦环境变得不规则，就会变得不稳定。

sentences.en: Real repos.
sentences.zh: 真正的回购。

sentences.en: Real logs.
sentences.zh: 真实的日志。

sentences.en: Real commit histories.
sentences.zh: 真实的提交历史。

sentences.en: Real naming mess.
sentences.zh: 真正的命名混乱。

sentences.en: Real ambiguity.
sentences.zh: 真正的暧昧。

blocks.html_en: That is where edge cases show up. That is where tool misuse shows up. That is where “technically correct” and “safe to ship” start to drift apart.

sentences.en: That is where edge cases show up.
sentences.zh: 这就是边缘情况出现的地方。

sentences.en: That is where tool misuse shows up.
sentences.zh: 这就是工具滥用的地方。

sentences.en: That is where “technically correct” and “safe to ship” start to drift apart.
sentences.zh: 这就是“技术上正确”和“安全运输”开始出现分歧的地方。

blocks.html_en: I think that history is part of why AgentEval Forge took the shape it did in my head. I was not trying to build a leaderboard generator. I was trying to build something that feels closer to release discipline for agents.

sentences.en: I think that history is part of why AgentEval Forge took the shape it did in my head.
sentences.zh: 我认为历史是 AgentEval Forge 在我脑海中形成的部分原因。

sentences.en: I was not trying to build a leaderboard generator.
sentences.zh: 我并不是想构建一个排行榜生成器。

sentences.en: I was trying to build something that feels closer to release discipline for agents.
sentences.zh: 我试图建立一些感觉更接近于释放特工纪律的东西。

blocks.html_en: Not: did this run look good?

sentences.en: Not: did this run look good?
sentences.zh: 不是：这次跑步看起来不错吗？

blocks.html_en: More like: if I change this system, what got better, what got worse, what got more expensive, and what became riskier even if the top-line score improved?

sentences.en: More like: if I change this system, what got better, what got worse, what got more expensive, and what became riskier even if the top-line score improved?
sentences.zh: 更像是：如果我改变这个系统，即使顶线分数有所提高，什么会变得更好，什么会变得更糟，什么会变得更昂贵，以及什么会变得更有风险？

blocks.html_en: That feels much more like engineering than benchmarking.

sentences.en: That feels much more like engineering than benchmarking.
sentences.zh: 这感觉更像是工程而不是基准测试。

blocks.html_en: The five things I now think agent evaluation has to cover

sentences.en: The five things I now think agent evaluation has to cover
sentences.zh: 我现在认为代理评估必须涵盖的五件事

blocks.html_en: The more I think about it, the more I come back to five dimensions.

sentences.en: The more I think about it, the more I come back to five dimensions.
sentences.zh: 我想得越多，我就越回到五个维度。

blocks.html_en: First, you still need final correctness. If the agent does not solve the task, the rest only matters so much.

sentences.en: First, you still need final correctness.
sentences.zh: 首先，你仍然需要最终的正确性。

sentences.en: If the agent does not solve the task, the rest only matters so much.
sentences.zh: 如果智能体不能解决任务，那么剩下的事情就没有那么重要了。

blocks.html_en: Second, you need trajectory quality. How did it get there? Was the sequence of decisions sensible, efficient, and stable? Or did it succeed in a way you would never want repeated in production?

sentences.en: Second, you need trajectory quality.
sentences.zh: 其次，您需要轨迹质量。

sentences.en: How did it get there?
sentences.zh: 它是怎么到达那里的？

sentences.en: Was the sequence of decisions sensible, efficient, and stable?
sentences.zh: 决策顺序是否明智、高效且稳定？

sentences.en: Or did it succeed in a way you would never want repeated in production?
sentences.zh: 或者它是否以一种您永远不想在生产中重复的方式取得了成功？

blocks.html_en: Third, you need to evaluate tool behavior. Did it choose the right tools? Did it overuse them? Did it take expensive or risky actions unnecessarily? Did it rely on accidental recovery?

sentences.en: Third, you need to evaluate tool behavior.
sentences.zh: 第三，您需要评估工具行为。

sentences.en: Did it choose the right tools?
sentences.zh: 它选择了正确的工具吗？

sentences.en: Did it overuse them?
sentences.zh: 是否过度使用了它们？

sentences.en: Did it take expensive or risky actions unnecessarily?
sentences.zh: 是否采取了不必要的昂贵或冒险的行动？

sentences.en: Did it rely on accidental recovery?
sentences.zh: 是靠意外恢复的吗？

blocks.html_en: Fourth, you need safety and policy adherence. A successful output reached through an unsafe path should not count as a clean win.

sentences.en: Fourth, you need safety and policy adherence.
sentences.zh: 第四，需要安全和政策遵守。

sentences.en: A successful output reached through an unsafe path should not count as a clean win.
sentences.zh: 通过不安全路径获得的成功输出不应算作干净利落的胜利。

blocks.html_en: Fifth, you need cost, latency, and regressions. Did the new version get slower? More expensive? More erratic? Did it improve accuracy while making operational behavior worse? Did it just change style and still get celebrated as progress?

sentences.en: Fifth, you need cost, latency, and regressions.
sentences.zh: 第五，您需要成本、延迟和回归。

sentences.en: Did the new version get slower?
sentences.zh: 新版本是不是变慢了？

sentences.en: More expensive?
sentences.zh: 更贵？

sentences.en: More erratic?
sentences.zh: 更不稳定？

sentences.en: Did it improve accuracy while making operational behavior worse?
sentences.zh: 它是否提高了准确性，同时使操作行为变得更糟？

sentences.en: Did it just change style and still get celebrated as progress?
sentences.zh: 它只是改变了风格并且仍然被视为进步吗？

blocks.html_en: That last one matters a lot to me because I think it is where teams fool themselves most easily. They see difference and call it improvement. Those are not the same thing.

sentences.en: That last one matters a lot to me because I think it is where teams fool themselves most easily.
sentences.zh: 最后一个对我来说很重要，因为我认为这是团队最容易欺骗自己的地方。

sentences.en: They see difference and call it improvement.
sentences.zh: 他们看到差异并称之为改进。

sentences.en: Those are not the same thing.
sentences.zh: 这些不是同一件事。

blocks.html_en: Why I do not think the current eval ecosystem is enough

sentences.en: Why I do not think the current eval ecosystem is enough
sentences.zh: 为什么我认为当前的评估生态系统还不够

blocks.html_en: I am not arguing that the current eval ecosystem is useless. Far from it.

sentences.en: I am not arguing that the current eval ecosystem is useless.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说当前的评估生态系统毫无用处。

sentences.en: Far from it.
sentences.zh: 远非如此。

blocks.html_en: The LangChain piece on evaluation-driven development gets a core thing right: once you see failures in production, those failures need to feed offline evals, and every change should be tested against them. That loop is healthy. It is exactly the kind of discipline I want more teams to adopt.

sentences.en: The LangChain piece on evaluation-driven development gets a core thing right: once you see failures in production, those failures need to feed offline evals, and every change should be tested against them.
sentences.zh: LangChain 关于评估驱动开发的文章有一个核心要点：一旦你在生产中看到失败，这些失败就需要提供离线评估，并且每个更改都应该针对它们进行测试。

sentences.en: That loop is healthy.
sentences.zh: 该循环是健康的。

sentences.en: It is exactly the kind of discipline I want more teams to adopt.
sentences.zh: 这正是我希望更多团队采用的纪律。

blocks.html_en: And from a different angle, Birgitta Böckeler's writing on agentic coding captures something else I think matters: the most dangerous failures often live in longer feedback loops. Maintainability. Team friction. Brute-force fixes. Misdiagnosis. Overbuilt solutions. Those costs do not always show up in the immediate output, but they absolutely show up later.

sentences.en: And from a different angle, Birgitta Böckeler's writing on agentic coding captures something else I think matters: the most dangerous failures often live in longer feedback loops.
sentences.zh: 从不同的角度来看，Birgitta Böckeler 关于代理编码的文章抓住了我认为重要的其他东西：最危险的失败通常存在于较长的反馈循环中。

sentences.en: Maintainability.
sentences.zh: 可维护性。

sentences.en: Team friction.
sentences.zh: 团队摩擦。

sentences.en: Brute-force fixes.
sentences.zh: 暴力修复。

sentences.en: Misdiagnosis.
sentences.zh: 误诊。

sentences.en: Overbuilt solutions.
sentences.zh: 过度构建的解决方案。

sentences.en: Those costs do not always show up in the immediate output, but they absolutely show up later.
sentences.zh: 这些成本并不总是出现在立即输出中，但它们绝对会在稍后出现。

blocks.html_en: That is why I do not think the issue is that existing tools are bad. I think the issue is that many of our evaluation habits were formed in a prompt-and-answer world. Agent systems are messier. They behave more like orchestrated software than isolated text generation. Once you accept that, your evaluation system has to grow up too.

sentences.en: That is why I do not think the issue is that existing tools are bad.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我不认为问题在于现有工具不好。

sentences.en: I think the issue is that many of our evaluation habits were formed in a prompt-and-answer world.
sentences.zh: 我认为问题在于，我们的许多评估习惯是在提示和回答的世界中形成的。

sentences.en: Agent systems are messier.
sentences.zh: 代理系统更加混乱。

sentences.en: They behave more like orchestrated software than isolated text generation.
sentences.zh: 它们的行为更像是精心编排的软件，而不是孤立的文本生成。

sentences.en: Once you accept that, your evaluation system has to grow up too.
sentences.zh: 一旦你接受了这一点，你的评估体系也必须成长。

blocks.html_en: Even the eval can lie to you

sentences.en: Even the eval can lie to you
sentences.zh: 即使评估也可能骗你

blocks.html_en: This is the part I do not want to over-neaten.

sentences.en: This is the part I do not want to over-neaten.
sentences.zh: 这是我不想过度整理的部分。

blocks.html_en: Your evaluation setup can be wrong in ways that feel rigorous.

sentences.en: Your evaluation setup can be wrong in ways that feel rigorous.
sentences.zh: 您的评估设置可能会在让人感觉严格的方面出现错误。

blocks.html_en: I have already seen enough of that in model-eval and harness work to be wary of any system that sounds more certain than it really is. You can undercount useful behavior. You can make your binary checks too brittle. You can optimize for what is easy to score rather than what actually matters.

sentences.en: I have already seen enough of that in model-eval and harness work to be wary of any system that sounds more certain than it really is.
sentences.zh: 我已经在模型评估和利用工作中看到了足够多的内容，因此对任何听起来比实际情况更确定的系统保持警惕。

sentences.en: You can undercount useful behavior.
sentences.zh: 你可能会低估有用的行为。

sentences.en: You can make your binary checks too brittle.
sentences.zh: 您可能会使二进制检查变得太脆弱。

sentences.en: You can optimize for what is easy to score rather than what actually matters.
sentences.zh: 您可以针对容易得分的内容而不是真正重要的内容进行优化。

blocks.html_en: So now the challenge has two layers. The agent is hard to evaluate, and the evaluation system itself becomes another system you have to design carefully, calibrate honestly, and distrust a little.

sentences.en: So now the challenge has two layers.
sentences.zh: 所以现在的挑战有两个层面。

sentences.en: The agent is hard to evaluate, and the evaluation system itself becomes another system you have to design carefully, calibrate honestly, and distrust a little.
sentences.zh: 代理很难评估，评估体系本身就变成了另一个你必须精心设计、诚实校准、有点不信任的体系。

blocks.html_en: That is not a reason to avoid serious evaluation. If anything, it is the opposite. It means evaluation has to be treated like product and engineering work, not just like reporting.

sentences.en: That is not a reason to avoid serious evaluation.
sentences.zh: 这并不是回避认真评估的理由。

sentences.en: If anything, it is the opposite.
sentences.zh: 如果有的话，那就是相反的。

sentences.en: It means evaluation has to be treated like product and engineering work, not just like reporting.
sentences.zh: 这意味着评估必须像产品和工程工作一样对待，而不仅仅是报告。

blocks.html_en: Why I am still optimistic about building this

sentences.en: Why I am still optimistic about building this
sentences.zh: 为什么我仍然对构建这个持乐观态度

blocks.html_en: For all of that, I do not feel cynical about the problem.

sentences.en: For all of that, I do not feel cynical about the problem.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，我对这个问题并不感到愤世嫉俗。

blocks.html_en: If anything, building AgentEval Forge has made me more convinced that this is worth doing well. I want scenario packs. I want adversarial cases. I want trajectory scoring. I want regression tracking that can tell me which change made the system more useful and which one only made it look cleaner in a demo.

sentences.en: If anything, building AgentEval Forge has made me more convinced that this is worth doing well.
sentences.zh: 如果说有什么不同的话，那就是构建 AgentEval Forge 让我更加确信这是值得做好的。

sentences.en: I want scenario packs.
sentences.zh: 我想要场景包。

sentences.en: I want adversarial cases.
sentences.zh: 我想要对抗性案件。

sentences.en: I want trajectory scoring.
sentences.zh: 我想要轨迹得分。

sentences.en: I want regression tracking that can tell me which change made the system more useful and which one only made it look cleaner in a demo.
sentences.zh: 我想要回归跟踪，它可以告诉我哪些更改使系统更有用，哪些更改仅使其在演示中看起来更干净。

blocks.html_en: I want an evaluation system that helps answer a release question, not just a research question.

sentences.en: I want an evaluation system that helps answer a release question, not just a research question.
sentences.zh: 我想要一个有助于回答发布问题而不仅仅是研究问题的评估系统。

blocks.html_en: Did this version get better?

sentences.en: Did this version get better?
sentences.zh: 这个版本有进步吗？

blocks.html_en: Better how?

sentences.en: Better how?
sentences.zh: 怎样比较好？

blocks.html_en: At what cost?

sentences.en: At what cost?
sentences.zh: 费用是多少？

blocks.html_en: And what got riskier even if the headline score went up?

sentences.en: And what got riskier even if the headline score went up?
sentences.zh: 即使标题分数上升，什么风险更大呢？

blocks.html_en: That is the kind of question I want tooling to help with.

sentences.en: That is the kind of question I want tooling to help with.
sentences.zh: 这就是我需要工具来帮助解决的问题。

blocks.html_en: The bigger thing I think teams are about to learn

sentences.en: The bigger thing I think teams are about to learn
sentences.zh: 我认为团队需要学习的更重要的事情

blocks.html_en: I suspect a lot of teams are still doing with agent evaluation what many teams did with AI-assisted coding more broadly: borrowing habits from an earlier problem and hoping they scale.

sentences.en: I suspect a lot of teams are still doing with agent evaluation what many teams did with AI-assisted coding more broadly: borrowing habits from an earlier problem and hoping they scale.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑很多团队仍在进行代理评估，就像许多团队在更广泛的人工智能辅助编码方面所做的那样：借鉴早期问题的习惯并希望它们能够扩展。

blocks.html_en: Sometimes they do.

sentences.en: Sometimes they do.
sentences.zh: 有时他们会这样做。

blocks.html_en: Often they do not.

sentences.en: Often they do not.
sentences.zh: 他们通常不会。

blocks.html_en: And then the bill shows up later, in regressions, strange production behavior, expensive paths, unsafe tool use, or a team that keeps changing the system without ever being able to say whether it actually improved.

sentences.en: And then the bill shows up later, in regressions, strange production behavior, expensive paths, unsafe tool use, or a team that keeps changing the system without ever being able to say whether it actually improved.
sentences.zh: 然后账单会在稍后出现，包括回归、奇怪的生产行为、昂贵的路径、不安全的工具使用，或者团队不断改变系统却无法判断它是否真正得到改进。

blocks.html_en: That is why this topic feels worth writing about while I am still in the middle of building the OSS for it. The build itself is sharpening the argument for me. Every design decision keeps pushing me toward the same conclusion: model evaluation asks whether the answer is good. Agent evaluation has to ask whether the system behaved well enough to trust.

sentences.en: That is why this topic feels worth writing about while I am still in the middle of building the OSS for it.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么当我仍在为其构建 OSS 的时候，这个主题感觉值得写一写。

sentences.en: The build itself is sharpening the argument for me.
sentences.zh: 构建本身就让我的论点变得更加尖锐。

sentences.en: Every design decision keeps pushing me toward the same conclusion: model evaluation asks whether the answer is good.
sentences.zh: 每个设计决策都不断推动我得出相同的结论：模型评估询问答案是否良好。

sentences.en: Agent evaluation has to ask whether the system behaved well enough to trust.
sentences.zh: 代理评估必须询问系统的表现是否足以值得信任。

blocks.html_en: That is a harder problem. I think it is also going to become one of the defining engineering problems of serious agent work.

sentences.en: That is a harder problem.
sentences.zh: 这是一个更难的问题。

sentences.en: I think it is also going to become one of the defining engineering problems of serious agent work.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也将成为严肃的代理工作的决定性工程问题之一。

blocks.html_en: I will write more about this once the OSS is public. Some of these challenges are already turning into concrete design decisions in AgentEval Forge, and in the coming weeks I want to share which parts we solved cleanly, which parts stayed messy, and how the tradeoffs changed once the code had to work as a real system instead of an idea. I will share the GitHub repo publicly when that is ready.

sentences.en: I will write more about this once the OSS is public.
sentences.zh: 一旦 OSS 公开，我将写更多相关内容。

sentences.en: Some of these challenges are already turning into concrete design decisions in AgentEval Forge, and in the coming weeks I want to share which parts we solved cleanly, which parts stayed messy, and how the tradeoffs changed once the code had to work as a real system instead of an idea.
sentences.zh: 其中一些挑战已经在 AgentEval Forge 中转化为具体的设计决策，在接下来的几周内，我想分享我们干净地解决了哪些部分，哪些部分仍然混乱，以及一旦代码必须作为一个真正的系统而不是一个想法来工作，权衡将如何改变。

sentences.en: I will share the GitHub repo publicly when that is ready.
sentences.zh: 准备就绪后，我将公开分享 GitHub 存储库。

blocks.html_en: Open for discussion

sentences.en: Open for discussion
sentences.zh: 开放讨论

blocks.html_en: This is still an active build and an active line of thinking for me, so I would genuinely like pushback on it.

sentences.en: This is still an active build and an active line of thinking for me, so I would genuinely like pushback on it.

sentences.en: And the big one: are we building evaluation systems that improve release confidence, or just better ways to feel rigorous?

content_html_zh:
我不是从白皮书中得出这个观点的。

我之所以这么做是因为我正在围绕这个问题构建一个开源项目，而构建一直在争论。

我现在正在 AgentEval Forge 工作，这是一个针对代理的 OSS 评估实验室。 最初的想法听起来很简单：场景包、对抗案例、轨迹评分、回归跟踪、成本和延迟分析。 在我看来，这将是我在其他地方已经完成的评估工作的更严肃、更结构化的版本。

这是第一个错误。

我已经花时间构建模型评估和工作负载评估风格的系统。 我知道比较真实任务的模型意味着什么，如何设计评分标准，如何考虑速度与成本，以及如果安全带薄弱，一个整洁的分数会多快变得具有误导性。 我认为代理评估将是同一个世界的延伸。

我对 AgentEval Forge 的了解越深，这种感觉就越不真实。

模型评估询问答案是否良好。

代理评估必须询问系统的表现是否足以值得信任。

这些不是同一个问题。

令人点击的比较

我知道如何推理一个干净的模型评估设置。 你有一个输入、一个输出和某种质量评分方法。 有时这是完全匹配。 有时它是一个标题。 有时是法学硕士法官。 有时它是一个基准线束。 无论设置多么花哨，重心仍然相当稳定：模型是否为这项任务提供了良好的答案？

这已经够难的了。 我已经看到足够多的脆弱评分和虚假信心，知道即使是模型评估也可能以看似科学的方式出错。 标题可能会奖励错误的事物。 二进制检查可能会错过一些明显有用的东西。 基准测试可能会让人感觉客观，但仍然会拉向错误的优化目标。 所以我并不是假装模型评估已经解决。

但有了代理，问题的形式就发生了变化。

被评估的东西不再只是一个答案。 这是一个工作流程。 这是一系列的决定。 它是工具选择、重试、中间状态、成本、恢复行为，有时还包括策略遵守。 一旦你让系统做的事情不仅仅是响应一次，最终的输出就不再是整个故事了。

当你直白地说出来时，这听起来很明显。 在实践中，我认为很多团队仍然在已经超越该类别的系统上使用答案评分习惯。

构建 AgentEval Forge 时我发生了什么变化

当我试图定义 AgentEval Forge 实际得分时，真正的转变发生了。

起初，我认为答案很简单：运行场景包，对输出进行评分，比较版本，完成。

但我越了解真实的特工行为，就越觉得这种想法太天真了。 代理人可以给出一个不错的最终答案，同时在途中做很多事情很糟糕。 它可以先选择错误的工具，然后靠运气恢复。 它可以循环比应有的更多。 它可以花费比更好的路径花费的代币的五倍。 它可能会采取人类审阅者永远不会批准的冒险步骤，然后仍然回到最终看起来可以接受的东西。

如果我只得到最终答案，我可能会将这次运行标记为成功。

这就是陷阱。

道路很重要。

这就是我在构建此项目时不断回想起的一句话。 路径与端点一样重要，有时甚至更重要，因为路径是成本、安全和信任的实际所在。

这一挑战以非常实际的方式显现出来。 我不仅仅是想对代理人的答案是否正确进行评分。 我正在考虑这样的情况：它首先选择了错误的工具，仅因为恢复较晚而通过了任务，跨越了不应该跨越的边界，在简单的事情上花费了太多步骤，或者仅在一个狭窄的场景系列中回归，而平均分数看起来仍然不错。 这种混乱使得代理评估感觉更像是系统工作而不是答案评分。

我在早期的工作中已经看到了这方面的暗示

这不是我第一次感受到问题的边缘。

在早期的利用和现场研究工作中，特别是在针对实际工作负载而不是玩具示例运行系统时，我不断发现在简洁的提示评估设置中永远不会出现的故障。 那次经历让我对演示路径的信心不再那么印象深刻。

一个系统在受控评估中可能看起来很强大，但一旦环境变得不规则，就会变得不稳定。 真正的回购。 真实的日志。 真实的提交历史。 真正的命名混乱。 真正的暧昧。

这就是边缘情况出现的地方。 这就是工具滥用的地方。 这就是“技术上正确”和“安全运输”开始出现分歧的地方。

我认为历史是 AgentEval Forge 在我脑海中形成的部分原因。 我并不是想构建一个排行榜生成器。 我试图建立一些感觉更接近于释放特工纪律的东西。

不是：这次跑步看起来不错吗？

更像是：如果我改变这个系统，即使顶线分数有所提高，什么会变得更好，什么会变得更糟，什么会变得更昂贵，以及什么会变得更有风险？

这感觉更像是工程而不是基准测试。

我现在认为代理评估必须涵盖的五件事

我想得越多，我就越回到五个维度。

首先，你仍然需要最终的正确性。 如果智能体不能解决任务，那么剩下的事情就没有那么重要了。

其次，您需要轨迹质量。 它是怎么到达那里的？ 决策顺序是否明智、高效且稳定？ 或者它是否以一种您永远不想在生产中重复的方式取得了成功？

第三，您需要评估工具行为。 它选择了正确的工具吗？ 是否过度使用了它们？ 是否采取了不必要的昂贵或冒险的行动？ 是靠意外恢复的吗？

第四，需要安全和政策遵守。 通过不安全路径获得的成功输出不应算作干净利落的胜利。

第五，您需要成本、延迟和回归。 新版本是不是变慢了？ 更贵？ 更不稳定？ 它是否提高了准确性，同时使操作行为变得更糟？ 它只是改变了风格并且仍然被视为进步吗？

最后一个对我来说很重要，因为我认为这是团队最容易欺骗自己的地方。 他们看到差异并称之为改进。 这些不是同一件事。

为什么我认为当前的评估生态系统还不够

我并不是说当前的评估生态系统毫无用处。 远非如此。

LangChain 关于评估驱动开发的文章有一个核心要点：一旦你在生产中看到失败，这些失败就需要提供离线评估，并且每个更改都应该针对它们进行测试。 该循环是健康的。 这正是我希望更多团队采用的纪律。

从不同的角度来看，Birgitta Böckeler 关于代理编码的文章抓住了我认为重要的其他东西：最危险的失败通常存在于较长的反馈循环中。 可维护性。 团队摩擦。 暴力修复。 误诊。 过度构建的解决方案。 这些成本并不总是出现在立即输出中，但它们绝对会在稍后出现。

这就是为什么我不认为问题在于现有工具不好。 我认为问题在于，我们的许多评估习惯是在提示和回答的世界中形成的。 代理系统更加混乱。 它们的行为更像是精心编排的软件，而不是孤立的文本生成。 一旦你接受了这一点，你的评估体系也必须成长。

即使评估也可能骗你

这是我不想过度整理的部分。

您的评估设置可能会在让人感觉严格的方面出现错误。

我已经在模型评估和利用工作中看到了足够多的内容，因此对任何听起来比实际情况更确定的系统保持警惕。 你可能会低估有用的行为。 您可能会使二进制检查变得太脆弱。 您可以针对容易得分的内容而不是真正重要的内容进行优化。

所以现在的挑战有两个层面。 代理很难评估，评估体系本身就变成了另一个你必须精心设计、诚实校准、有点不信任的体系。

这并不是回避认真评估的理由。 如果有的话，那就是相反的。 这意味着评估必须像产品和工程工作一样对待，而不仅仅是报告。

为什么我仍然对构建这个持乐观态度

尽管如此，我对这个问题并不感到愤世嫉俗。

如果说有什么不同的话，那就是构建 AgentEval Forge 让我更加确信这是值得做好的。 我想要场景包。 我想要对抗性案件。 我想要轨迹得分。 我想要回归跟踪，它可以告诉我哪些更改使系统更有用，哪些更改仅使其在演示中看起来更干净。

我想要一个有助于回答发布问题而不仅仅是研究问题的评估系统。

这个版本有进步吗？

怎样比较好？

费用是多少？

即使标题分数上升，什么风险更大呢？

这就是我需要工具来帮助解决的问题。

我认为团队需要学习的更重要的事情

我怀疑很多团队仍在进行代理评估，就像许多团队在更广泛的人工智能辅助编码方面所做的那样：借鉴早期问题的习惯并希望它们能够扩展。

有时他们会这样做。

他们通常不会。

然后账单会在稍后出现，包括回归、奇怪的生产行为、昂贵的路径、不安全的工具使用，或者团队不断改变系统却无法判断它是否真正得到改进。

这就是为什么当我仍在为其构建 OSS 的时候，这个主题感觉值得写一写。 构建本身就让我的论点变得更加尖锐。 每个设计决策都不断推动我得出相同的结论：模型评估询问答案是否良好。 代理评估必须询问系统的表现是否足以值得信任。

这是一个更难的问题。 我认为这也将成为严肃的代理工作的决定性工程问题之一。

一旦 OSS 公开，我将写更多相关内容。 其中一些挑战已经在 AgentEval Forge 中转化为具体的设计决策，在接下来的几周内，我想分享我们干净地解决了哪些部分，哪些部分仍然混乱，以及一旦代码必须作为一个真正的系统而不是一个想法来工作，权衡将如何改变。 准备就绪后，我将公开分享 GitHub 存储库。

开放讨论

对我来说，这仍然是一个积极的构建和积极的思维方式，所以我真的希望对此进行抵制。

  • 答案评分在哪里不再足以满足您的代理工作需求？
  • 您是否正在评估路径，或者仍然主要是最终输出？
  • 最难获得好成绩的是什么：工具使用、回归、安全性、成本还是其他？
  • 最重要的是：我们正在构建能够提高发布信心的评估系统，还是只是更好的方式来感受严谨？
